evidence.curator_note: Upper branch of Equation 8.56, on the reaction arrow labelled 'i' (inductive / charge-site cleavage) leaving the ring-opened distonic ion .CH2CH2CH2CH2-O+=CH2: the oxocarbenium O1-C6 bond breaks heterolytically with both electrons migrating to the charge-bearing oxygen, expelling neutral formaldehyde (printed as 'O=CH2') and leaving the hydrocarbon C4H8+. ion at m/z 56, 55%. Book draws 0 arcs for this branch (only the italic 'i' reaction arrow); the single double-barbed arrow encoded here is curator-supplied for electron balance. DRAWN-STRUCTURE DISCLOSURE: the page draws the m/z 56 ion as a four-membered ring with THREE solid bonds and a DOTTED 1,4-bond, '+' on one terminus and '.' on the other, i.e. the tetramethylene distonic radical cation +CH2CH2CH2CH2. caught on the way to the cyclobutane radical cation. A partial (dotted) bond has no SMILES representation, so the open-chain distonic form that the arrow actually produces is encoded and the incipient ring closure is disclosed here.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no entry for 8.56 (its chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14); no MØD rule variable is cross-linked to this scheme. The only indexed ring-opening/ring-fragmentation family, IMS_8_6_1..IMS_8_6_4, is an all-carbon cyclooctadiene rule with no heteroatom and no C-O heterolysis, so it does NOT match this inductive CH2O loss. The page prints abundances as bare percentages without naming the experiment; they are the book's standard 70 eV EI values, and ms_context is set accordingly. The species undergoing this step is the ring-opened isomer of the molecular ion (same C5H10O+. composition, m/z 86), so adduct is kept as [M]+•.
